  • Damn cool old car

  • Interior needs completely replaced, which I would do near the end of the project

As a project, I would say yes. They are like having the most elaborate go-cart ever.

In my youth I had a 67 Austin Healey Sprite. Basically the exact same car. It was one fun car to drive and own. They're basically simple mechanically. The carburetors can be a bitch though, so beware. Biggest thing to watch for is the electrical system on this, or any English Roadster type. The Lucas electrical system is well know as 'Lucas, prince of darkness', so checkout the electrical ... lights, wiring, all that kind of stuff thoroughly. But simply put, I've owner three English roasters ... the Sprite, a Healey 3000 and an MGB. I enjoyed them all, but all require someone who likes to play around mechanically from time to time. Fun wise, though ... they can't be beat. The Midget is the bottom of the line as far as performance and such, but is fast enough, and breezes around the road with no problems. There's nothing like a good top down summer ride ... but one other drawback, depending on where you live, they aren't good at all in winter weather. You say it won't be a daily driver, but if you do drive it a lot, plan to park it when the snow flies.

BTW, checkout your local area. There are generally British car clubs everywhere and are a ball to join and hang out with. They do things like drives to here or there and meets and such. Can be fun. Oh, and parts tend to be on the expensive side ... checkout Victoria British ... it was my go to for parts and one of the better ones. You'll at lest have an idea of what stuff may cost you by paging through their site.

Good luck, and have fun! I really enjoyed my roadsters ... fun times were had by all.
